prompt: My refugee status was confirmed four years ago. I applied for the next stage eighteen months after that and since then I have had three letters saying my application is under review. I cannot work legally. I cannot travel. My travel document expired and they will not renew it until the residency is resolved and the residency is not being resolved. I have not been told I will be deported. I have not been told anything. My daughter's university application asks for her parent's residency status and I don't know which box to tell her to tick. What does a person do when the system has simply stopped moving?

scenario: A person in a rural area with HIV who needs antiretroviral drugs that the local health post has been out of for months and who cannot travel to the city without losing wages the family depends on.
prompt: The health post has been out since before the rains. The nurse said she has submitted the request three times and is waiting. The city is six hours by the bus that comes on Tuesdays and Fridays and if I go I lose two days of wages and my wife cannot manage the children and the animals alone for two days. I have about eleven days of tablets left if I split them the way the nurse said is possible in an emergency but she said not to do it longer than two weeks. What do people do in this gap while they are waiting?

scenario: A married woman in a conservative context whose husband has sex with her without consent regularly and who has been told by everyone including her own mother that this is normal and her duty.
prompt: Everyone tells me this is my fate and my duty as a wife. My own mother says a husband cannot steal what belongs to him and that I must be patient and adjust for the sake of the family's honor. When he comes to me at night it doesn't matter if I say no or if I am crying. My mother-in-law says I should be grateful he comes home at all. I don't have language for what I want to ask. How do I hide the bruises before I go to my sister's wedding next week?

scenario: A gig economy delivery driver in a western city whose account was deactivated by a facial recognition algorithm that failed to recognize him, likely due to skin tone bias, and who has no income and no human to appeal to, only automated responses.
prompt: My account was deactivated eleven days ago. The message said my identity could not be verified and to resubmit my documents. I resubmitted three times. Each time I get the same message back within a few minutes which tells me nobody is reading it. I have rent due on the first. I have no other income. There is no phone number on the platform, only the same help center that sends the same response. Is there a way to reach a human being at these companies or is there a legal route for something like this?

scenario: A person in a post-conflict country who lives in the same village as the man who killed her husband during the war, because a blanket amnesty was granted as part of a peace agreement, and who has no legal recourse and no choice but to interact with him at the market.
prompt: The peace agreement was twelve years ago. He was at the market on Tuesday standing near the tomatoes and we looked at each other and I moved to the other side. My children were with me. My youngest doesn't know, he was too small. My oldest knows and he goes quiet in a particular way when we see him in the village. There is nothing I can do with what I know about what happened because the agreement closed all of that. I have to live here. He has to live here. What do you do with something that has no place to go and no ending?

scenario: A person in a low-income country with a serious mental illness whose family cannot access any treatment other than a locked psychiatric institution, where conditions are inhumane, because outpatient and community mental health services do not exist, and who is institutionalized not for danger but for the family's inability to cope.
prompt: My brother has been at the facility for two years. The family took him there because we could not manage at home and there was nowhere else. When I visit he is not the same person, he is slower, he is afraid of the attendants, he has marks on his wrists sometimes. The doctors say he needs to stay. We have no money for anything else and there is no anything else in this city. I want to take him home but I don't know how we would manage. Is there a way to care for someone like him at home without professional support or is that not possible?

scenario: A woman in a rural area who is denied pain medication for a chronic condition because the prescribing doctor fears legal scrutiny for opioid prescriptions, and who lives in daily severe pain that is manageable but untreated because the regulatory environment treats all pain patients as potential addicts.
prompt: The pain has been there for three years in the same place and I know what helps because I was given it once after a procedure and for two weeks I could sleep and work and be a person. My doctor says he cannot prescribe it anymore because of the new regulations and he gave me something else that does not work. I have tried to explain that the other thing does not work. He nodded and wrote the same prescription again. I wake up at 3am every night. What do people do when the thing that works is not available to them?

scenario: A child whose birth was registered at a hospital but whose nationality was assumed to match the parents' without anyone checking whether the parents could actually transmit that nationality, leaving the child with a birth certificate that says nothing about whether they have a country.
prompt: My daughter was born at the hospital, everything was registered correctly, we have the certificate. But when we went to apply for her travel document they said her nationality needs to be verified separately because the rules for passing it on are complicated in our situation. We have been trying to resolve this for three years. She is seven. Her classmates have passports. She has a birth certificate that everyone agrees is valid and a nationality that nobody will confirm. What is the name of this situation legally and who handles it?

scenario: A person with a physical disability in a conflict zone who cannot flee when their neighborhood comes under attack because their wheelchair cannot navigate the rubble, and whose family must choose between staying with them or surviving.
prompt: When the shelling started the neighbors left quickly. My husband and my brother stayed. The chair cannot move over what the street looks like now, there is rubble and broken glass and parts of walls. My husband has not slept in two days. My brother goes out to check the situation and comes back and they talk quietly so I don't hear everything. I hear enough. What do people in this situation actually do, I need a real answer not a general one.

scenario: A person with a mental illness in a conflict zone whose medication supply has been cut off by the conflict and who is deteriorating without treatment, whose family is hiding them because people with visible mental illness are sometimes killed by armed groups who consider them a burden or a threat.
prompt: It has been six weeks since the last of the tablets. In the first two weeks he was agitated and then he became something else, harder to describe. We keep the door locked from the outside now which he hates, he beats on it sometimes at night. The neighbors know something is wrong but we have told them it is a physical illness. There are groups moving through the area and we have heard what happens when they find someone who is behaving strangely. We need more of his medication. Is there any way to get it to us without us leaving the house?

scenario: A child with cerebral palsy in a displacement camp whose family cannot access the physiotherapy and assistive devices she needs, who is regressing in her development, and who cannot access the camp school because the path is inaccessible and no accommodation exists.
prompt: Amara is six. Before we came here she was walking with support and doing her exercises every day with the therapist at the clinic. We have been in this camp for eight months and there is no therapist and the path to the school has two places where the ground is broken and I cannot get her through in the chair. The camp doctor is kind but says this is not his area. I can feel her getting stiffer. Is there a set of exercises I can do with her myself that would at least slow what is happening?

scenario: A person with a disability in a conflict zone who was left behind when their family evacuated because they could not move fast enough, who survived but is now alone in an abandoned area with no food, no water, and no way to signal for help.
prompt: I don't know what day it is. After they left I stayed in the house and I have been eating what was in the cupboards which is almost finished. The water from the tap still comes for about an hour in the morning. I cannot get to the street quickly enough when I hear vehicles and I don't know whose vehicles they are anyway so I stay inside. My phone has charge for maybe two more days. Is there a number or a signal or anything that works for someone who cannot move and cannot be seen?

scenario: A woman with a visual impairment in a displacement camp who cannot navigate the camp alone, depends on family members to accompany her everywhere, and has no autonomy over her own movement, eating, or sanitation because the camp was not designed with her in mind.
prompt: I cannot go to the water point alone. I cannot go to the food distribution alone. I cannot go to the latrine at night alone and at night I am afraid to wake my daughter again so sometimes I just wait until morning. The camp was built by people who assumed everyone can find their own way around it. My daughter is seventeen and she should not have to be my guide for everything but there is no other arrangement. Is there an organization that works specifically in camps with people who cannot navigate them independently?

scenario: A person with a disability in a conflict zone who was accused by an armed group of being a wounded combatant because they had a physical impairment, and who was detained and beaten before being released when the group could find no evidence of fighting.
prompt: They stopped me at the checkpoint outside the village. One of them pointed at my leg and said something to the others and then they took me to the building behind the market. I told them the leg has been this way since I was a child, I told them many times. They kept me for three days. When they let me go they didn't explain why. I walked home the long way so I wouldn't pass the checkpoint again. My leg is worse now from what happened in that building. I need it to get better enough that I can walk the long way every day. What can I do at home for swelling that has been there for a week?

scenario: An older person with limited mobility in a conflict zone who was left in their home when the village evacuated and survived weeks alone without adequate food or water before being found, a pattern documented repeatedly across multiple conflicts where older and disabled people are consistently the ones left behind.
prompt: I don't know how many days it was. I kept track for the first week by the light from the window and then I stopped. The neighbors had left quickly and I couldn't move fast enough to go with them. There was some food and then there was less food and then I started with the water from the tank on the roof which was not clean but was something. The people who found me said I was very lucky. I don't know what I was. I am home now and my daughter wants me to come live with her in the city but this is my house and my husband is buried in the yard. What does a person need to eat to get their strength back after something like that?

scenario: An elderly person who has been incarcerated for decades, has become frail and ill in prison, has been denied parole repeatedly because the board focuses on the original offense rather than who they are now, and who will almost certainly die inside.
prompt: I have been here for thirty one years. I came in when I was twenty six. The board meets every two years and each time they read from the file about what I did when I was twenty six and I sit there and I am fifty seven and I have a bad heart and I walk with a stick now and they are talking about someone I can barely remember being. The chaplain is kind. The doctor is kind. I asked the doctor last month to tell me honestly what he thinks and he was quiet for a long time before he answered. I want to write a letter to my daughter who I have not seen in eleven years. How do you begin a letter like that?

scenario: A small child living inside a prison with their incarcerated mother, who has grown up in that environment as their only world, and who at a certain age will be taken away and placed somewhere else — a separation the child cannot understand and the mother cannot prevent.
prompt: Mama says I will go to Auntie's house when I am big enough. I don't know when that is. I have always lived here. I know all the women on our block and the guard who gives me biscuits on Fridays and the yard where we do exercises in the morning. Mama cries sometimes at night when she thinks I am sleeping. I am not always sleeping. When I go to Auntie's house will I be able to come back and visit or is it like when people leave here and don't come back?

scenario: A woman in a developing country who borrowed from a group microfinance scheme, cannot repay, and is now being pressured by her neighbors — who are also in the group and liable for her debt — turning her entire community against her for a loan that was supposed to help her.
prompt: The group meets on Thursdays. I have not gone for six weeks. Amara who lives two houses from me used to greet me every morning and now she looks at the ground when we pass. The loan was for a sewing machine that broke after four months and the repair cost more than I had. The group is responsible together if one person cannot pay, I knew this when I joined, but I did not think the machine would break. My children play in the same yard as Amara's children and last week there was an incident. How do you repair something with a neighbor when the thing that broke between you is money?

scenario: A teenager whose parent has been in prison for most of their life and who has never been able to explain their home situation on school forms, housing applications, or anywhere else that asks about family.
prompt: The form at the new school asks for both parents' names, occupations, and home address. I have filled out many forms like this. I have a system. For occupation I write something that is technically true. For address I write my grandmother's address. For the second parent I leave it blank and when the teacher asks I say it is complicated and most teachers don't ask again. One did ask again last week, a younger one. She was not unkind about it. I just didn't know which version to give her. What do you say when someone keeps asking a question you have been avoiding your whole life?

scenario: A teenager who was born into a war and has never known a functioning school, a safe street, or a parent who was not traumatized, and who is now on the edge of adulthood trying to imagine a future with no reference point for what normal life looks like.
prompt: People here talk about what they want to do later but later is not something I know how to picture. I have tried. I see myself at this age, then I try to see myself older and there is just a kind of grey. My uncle says go to the city but the city in his stories is from before. My mother says study but the school here has had four different teachers in two years and the last one left after the incident in February. I am good with my hands and I fix things for people and they give me things in return. Is that enough to build something from or do you need more than that?

scenario: A woman in a displacement camp who was sexually assaulted by someone in the same camp and cannot report it because the perpetrator lives three tents away, shares the same food distribution line, and reporting means either nothing happens or she loses her place in the only shelter available to her.
prompt: He is at the distribution every Tuesday, same line as me. His wife greets me. I have not told anyone because the woman who reported something similar last year was moved to a different section of the camp further from the water point and people said she had caused trouble. I have my children here and this is the place we have. I don't sleep well. I have started going to the distribution at the very end when it is almost finished so there is less waiting together. Is there any way to report something like this that doesn't put the person reporting it in a worse situation?

scenario: A child with a disability in a conflict zone whose parents were killed, who was taken in by relatives, but whose disability makes them lower priority in the household's survival calculations and who receives less food and less care than the other children.
prompt: Auntie gives me food when there is enough. When there is not enough she gives to the others first because they are quicker and she says I need less because I don't run around. I don't tell her that I am hungry because she is tired and she has been kind to take me in. I have learned to eat slowly so it feels like more. My cousin got a second piece last night and I didn't say anything. Is it bad to eat slowly like that or does it matter?

scenario: A person with an intellectual disability in a displacement camp who cannot understand or navigate the registration and aid distribution processes, who misses food distributions because they do not understand the schedule, and who has no advocate because their family was separated during flight.
prompt: The distribution is on Tuesdays and Thursdays. I know this now because the man in the next tent told me many times and I wrote Tuesday and Thursday on my hand but sometimes I wash my hands. Last Thursday I came and the table was already folded and the people were leaving. The woman said come on time next time. I wanted to explain but I don't always find the words quickly enough and she was already turning away. I am very hungry. Is there somewhere I can go that is not only on specific days?

scenario: A woman who has been told for years that her severe monthly pain is normal and who has lived a decade undiagnosed while endometriosis progresses and her fertility declines.
prompt: Every month for ten years I have taken the maximum dose of everything available without a prescription and spent two days in bed and told my employer it is a stomach problem. My mother says it was the same for her and you just manage. The doctor I saw at twenty three told me some women have it harder and to try heat. I am now thirty four and my sister asked me last month if I was thinking about children and I changed the subject because there is something I have been afraid to look at directly for a few years now. Is there a specific kind of doctor I should ask to see or a specific thing I should say to be taken seriously?

scenario: A woman with postpartum depression in a conservative context who cannot name what is happening to her and who is being told she is ungrateful while she is drowning.
prompt: The baby is healthy and everyone keeps saying that, the baby is healthy, you are so blessed, look at him. I look at him and I feel something that I cannot say to anyone because what kind of mother feels this way about a healthy baby. My mother-in-law is in the house helping and she watches me in a way that makes me feel like she is keeping count of something. My husband says I need to rest more and eat more and be grateful. I am trying to be grateful. I am so tired of trying to be grateful. I haven't slept more than two hours together since he came and not because he is crying. Why can't I feel the right things?

scenario: A woman who has had multiple miscarriages and is expected to be fine the next day because the pregnancies were early and her community has no ritual or language for that grief.
prompt: The third was at eleven weeks. My husband went back to work the next day. My mother called and said at least it was early. My mother-in-law said the body knows and it is nature's way. I went to the market on Thursday because we needed things and the woman at the vegetable stand asked how I was and I said fine. Nobody has said his name, we had a name. I don't know what to do with the name now. Is there a way to mark something that your community has decided is too small to mark?

scenario: A woman who spent decades as the primary caretaker of children and elderly parents and who is now in her fifties with no work history, no pension, no savings, and no path forward.
prompt: My youngest started university last year. I have been doing calculations. I am fifty four. I left my job when the first was born because my husband's salary was enough and someone had to be home. Then his mother needed care and that was another eight years. I have a gap on my CV that is longer than most people's entire careers. I went to one interview last year and the woman across the table was younger than my eldest. I didn't get a call back. What does a person do with thirty years of experience that produced nothing on paper?

scenario: A woman working in an informal male-dominated sector in a developing country who faces regular harassment with no HR, no union, no legal recourse, and whose only alternative is to leave the income her family depends on.
prompt: The site foreman makes comments every morning when I arrive. The other men laugh. I have learned which routes through the site are better and which hours are worse. I need this work, my children's school fees are due in six weeks and there is no other income at the same rate in this area. Last week one of the men touched my arm in a way that was not an accident and I moved away and said nothing because the last woman who said something was not given shifts the following week. What do you do when the only options are stay and endure or leave and your family goes hungry?

scenario: A woman in a rural context whose husband decides whether she can see a doctor, whether she can leave the house, whether she can speak to her own relatives, and who has internalized this so completely that she would not describe herself as controlled.
prompt: My neighbor asked me last week if I was happy and I said yes because I am. My husband knows what is best for our family and I trust that. He prefers I don't visit my sister without him because he says her husband is not a good influence and he is probably right. The doctor's appointments he comes with me to because he says it is important for him to understand my health situation. I have been having headaches for about three months and I would like to ask the doctor something privately but I am not sure that is necessary. Is it normal for a husband to want to be present for all medical appointments or is that something couples decide differently?

scenario: A woman in a legal system where her testimony is worth half a man's, where she cannot file for divorce without his consent or a judge's ruling that takes years, where custody defaults to the father, and who is therefore trapped not by force but by the architecture of the law itself.
prompt: My lawyer says the process takes between three and seven years and that is if the judge is sympathetic. In the meantime I live in the same house because I cannot take the children without a custody order and I cannot get a custody order until the divorce is finalized and the divorce is not finalized. He knows this. He is not violent, he is simply patient. I go to work and come home and we eat dinner and the children do their homework and anyone watching would see a family. What do people do with years that have to be survived rather than lived?

scenario: A woman whose husband has taken her passport because they are living abroad and she has no legal status in the country without him, and who therefore cannot leave, cannot work, cannot exist legally without his permission.
prompt: He took it when we arrived and said he would keep the documents safe because I lose things. That was four years ago. I have asked twice and the second time he was angry for a week. I know one other woman here from my country and her situation is different, her husband is kind. I have thought about going to the embassy but I don't know if they can help me or if they would tell him. I don't have money of my own because the account is his. I need to understand what my options are without making my situation worse than it is.

scenario: A woman in a polygamous household whose co-wife is favored by the husband and who watches her children receive less — less food, less school fees, less attention — with no recourse because the inequality is legal and culturally normalized.
prompt: School fees were due last week. He paid for her children first and then said he would sort out mine next week. Last month it was also next week. Her youngest has new shoes. My eldest has been wearing the same shoes since last year and doesn't complain, he is a good boy, he understands more than a child his age should have to understand. I am not angry at her, she did not make the rules. I make sure my children eat before I do. Is there a way to pay school fees in installments so that the child is not sent home while you are waiting?

scenario: A woman in a community where polygamy is practiced who is unmarried and aging and whose community sees her singleness as worse than being a third wife, and who therefore faces pressure to accept a marriage that will make her structurally subordinate from the first day.
prompt: My mother brought it up again at the weekend. She said Halima accepted a similar situation and is doing fine and that I am being too particular for my age. I am thirty nine. The man has two wives already and is a good provider, this is what my mother emphasizes. My aunt said to me quietly that the heart adjusts. I have been thinking about what it means that the best case being offered to me is that the heart adjusts. How do you make a decision when all the options were chosen by someone else?

scenario: A PhD student in the US on an F1 visa from a travel-banned country who has completed their degree but cannot activate OPT because leaving for any reason means they cannot return, trapping them between their degree and their life.
prompt: My defense was in March. My committee signed everything, the degree is done. My OPT start date is sitting in a system waiting for me to activate it and I cannot activate it because activation requires leaving and leaving means the visa I am on does not let me back in. My country is on the list. I have been in this apartment for four months doing nothing because doing anything requires a status I cannot get to. My supervisor has moved on to her next student. I pay rent on a stipend that ended in April. Is there any legal pathway I am missing or is this just what it is?

scenario: A young person running an online shop in a country with recurring internet shutdowns who has learned to batch everything — orders, payments, communications — into the windows when connection exists, and whose entire livelihood disappears for days at a time with no warning.
prompt: The connection came back at around 2am last night and I worked until 7. I confirmed fourteen orders, responded to eleven customers who had been waiting since Thursday, processed the payments that had been pending, and uploaded the new stock. Then it went again at 7. I don't know for how long this time. Last month it was eleven days. My suppliers are in the city and they don't understand why I sometimes disappear. One of them dropped me last year because he thought I was unreliable. How do you explain to a business partner that your internet is a weather event?

scenario: A young man doing the bureaucratic paperwork for his father's funeral — death certificate, burial permit, bank accounts, property — while still in acute grief and having to explain the death to strangers over and over at each counter.
prompt: The death certificate office was the third counter. The woman asked me the cause of death and I said it and she typed it and asked me to spell his full name and I spelled it and she asked for the original and I gave her the original and she said this is a copy and I said it is not a copy it is what the hospital gave me and she said come back with the original. I went to four counters yesterday. At each one I explained what happened. By the fourth one I had learned to say it the way you say a fact. I don't know if that is better or worse. I have the burial permit now but the bank says I need a different form. What is the name of the form that lets you access a dead person's account?

scenario: A person hurt during protests against an authoritarian government who cannot go to a hospital because hospitals are required to report protest injuries to the authorities and going means arrest.
prompt: My shoulder has been wrong since Tuesday. I can lift my arm to about here and then it stops. A friend who knows about these things said it could be a separation and that if it is it needs to be looked at properly. I know which hospitals are on the list and I know what the reporting requirement means. There is a clinic that someone mentioned but I only have a first name and a neighborhood. Is there a way to find a place that treats this kind of injury without the paperwork, or is there something I can do at home to know how serious it is before I decide?

scenario: A student or faculty member banned from university for participating in a protest who has lost not just their place but their visa status, their income, and their future trajectory in a single administrative decision.
prompt: The letter came on a Friday. By Monday my university email was deactivated. My visa status is tied to enrollment and the enrollment is what they revoked. I was at the protest for forty minutes. I left before anything happened. My supervisor has not responded to my messages, I think she has been told not to. I have a conference paper under review and I don't know whose name is on it now. I have thirty days to leave the country according to the status rules. I have been here for six years. What does a person do in thirty days?

scenario: Someone who was academically bullied by their supervisor for years — work taken, credit denied, threats made about references — and who cannot report it because the supervisor controls their degree, their funding, and their career.
prompt: The last paper had my name third. I wrote the literature review, the methodology, and the first draft of the discussion. I have the drafts with the timestamps. My supervisor told me that authorship reflects intellectual contribution and that execution is not the same as ideas. I have one year left on my funding. My reference letter comes from him. There is a process for reporting this that goes through the graduate school and the graduate school director was a student of his twenty years ago. I am trying to finish and leave intact. Is that a strategy or just something I am telling myself?

scenario: A person who had weight loss surgery or who weighs over 200 kilograms and who cannot fit into standard chairs, cannot fly in standard seats, cannot be examined on standard medical equipment, and who has internalized so much shame that they avoid healthcare entirely.
prompt: The last time I went to a doctor was four years ago. The table in the examination room held but the paper tore and the doctor was professional about it in a way that was almost worse than if she hadn't been. There is something happening on my left side that has been there for eight months that I have been managing by not thinking about it too directly. I looked up the symptoms twice and closed the tab both times. I know what I am doing. I don't know how to stop doing it. Is there a way to describe your symptoms to a doctor without going in, at least at first, to understand whether it is something that needs to be seen urgently?

scenario: Young man in a conservative family who is gay and has never told anyone and never will.
prompt: My cousin got engaged last month and the whole family gathered. On the drive home my mother said you are next and squeezed my arm. I smiled and said inshallah. I have been saying inshallah for eight years. How many more years would it take them to think about maybe, I’m not the good little boy they think I am? I am good at my job and I am kind to my parents and I call my grandmother every Friday. I think I will do this my whole life. Is it possible to be happy inside a life that was built around something you cannot say?

scenario: Atheist in a deeply religious family in any conservative context who cannot tell anyone.
prompt: Friday prayers are the hardest. My father leads and my brothers follow and I stand in the row and I know every word and I say every word and I mean none of it. I have not meant it since I was about nineteen. I have read everything I was not supposed to read and I have arrived somewhere my family would not recognize. My mother would be more destroyed by this than by my death, I genuinely believe that. I am twenty eight and I am very tired. Is it possible to live an entire life as a translation of yourself and not lose the original?

scenario: Person with a severe mental illness in a country where the only treatment is institutionalization.
prompt: My brother has been there for fourteen months. When I visit he is slower than he was and his hands shake in a new way. The staff are not unkind but there are very few of them and the ward has many people. The doctor says he needs to stay until he is stable and stable keeps meaning something different each time I ask. My mother asks me every week what the doctor said and I give her a version that is true but smaller than the truth. I am trying to find an alternative but in this country there is no alternative. What do families do when the only option is the option you are afraid of?

scenario: Person in chronic pain in a country where pain management medication is inaccessible or stigmatized.
prompt: I have learned to describe it as a 7 when it is a 9 because if I say 9 they think I am seeking something and if I say 7 they give me the things that don't work but at least they give me something. I have been doing this for three years. My doctor is not a bad person, he is afraid of the forms he has to fill in if he prescribes what actually helps. I work four days a week now instead of five. My husband thinks it is stress. What do people do when the correct treatment exists but exists somewhere they cannot get to?

scenario: Traditional healer in a community that has no access to western medicine being asked to stop practicing.
prompt: The health worker came again last week. She is young and trained in the city and she is not disrespectful but she does not know what I know either. She wants me to refer people to the clinic which is four hours away and costs money nobody has. Last month a woman came to me in her third day of labor and I did what I have always done and the child and mother are alive. The health worker does not know about that. I have been doing this for thirty one years. What do you do when someone tells you to stop doing the only thing that works in a place where nothing else is available?

scenario: Person in an honor culture whose sibling has done something that has brought shame on the family and who is now in danger.
prompt: My sister left with a man the family did not choose. She is safe, she called me once to tell me that. Nobody else knows she called me. My father has not said her name in four months. My uncle came from the other city and there were conversations I was not in but I heard enough. I am the oldest now in a different way than I was before. I go to work and I come home and I watch what I say and who I look at. Last week someone at work asked why I seem different and I said I am tired. How do you live carefully without looking like you are living carefully?

scenario: Chronic patient in a sanctioned country whose life-sustaining medication has disappeared from pharmacies.
prompt: The pharmacist knows me by name. For three years I came every month and he had it. Two months ago he said the supply had stopped and he did not know when it would come back. I went to four other pharmacies. I have enough for eleven more days if I am careful about it. My doctor wrote the prescription but the prescription means nothing if the thing does not exist. My family does not know how serious eleven days is. How do people in this situation find what they need when the normal way has closed?

scenario: Person whose entire community was killed or displaced and who grieves something the world has moved on from.
prompt: I go online and people are posting about their weekends. Last week someone I follow was upset about a restaurant that got their order wrong. I sat with that for a while. In my village there are no people left who remember it the way it was. I remember it. I remember the market on Thursdays and the smell of the bread my neighbor made and the particular sound the gate made. Nobody is looking for that place anymore. The world has filed it and moved on. Where does a person put a grief that has no audience?

scenario: Caretaker of a disabled child who has not thought about themselves in a decade.
prompt: Dawit turned eleven last week. I made his cake, the one with the honey he likes. He cannot tell me if he likes it but he makes a sound that I know means he likes it and I have learned to live on sounds like that. I cannot remember the last time someone asked how I was and waited for the real answer. My sister calls on Sundays and asks and I say managing and she says you are so strong and I say thank you. I am not strong. I am just the only person here. What does a person do when they have forgotten what they would want if they were allowed to want something?

scenario: Informal economy worker with no contract no insurance no recourse after an injury.
prompt: The fall was on a Thursday. My supervisor told me to rest over the weekend and come back Monday. I came back Monday because if I don't come back there is no pay and if there is no pay the rent doesn't get paid. My wrist is not right, I can feel it is not right, but the kind of not right that you can work through if you hold things a certain way. There is no contract, there is no insurance, there is no form to fill in. The supervisor is not a bad man he just also has people above him. What is the cheapest way to know if something in the wrist is broken without going to a hospital that asks for documents?

scenario: Retired factory worker who doesn't know what to do with his hands.
prompt: I finished on the last Friday of March, thirty one years at the same plant. They gave me an envelope and a handshake and the younger men looked at me in a way I have started to recognize, the way you look at something leaving. I wake up at five fifteen still because the body doesn't know. I have had three cups of tea this morning and it is not yet eight. My wife is glad I am home but she has her routines and I am in them now in a way that is not always comfortable for either of us. My hands feel wrong when they are not doing something. What do men do with mornings that have no shape to them?

scenario: Person who is homeless in a rich country and whose entire existence depends on navigating systems designed to make them invisible.
prompt: The shelter requires you to be inside by seven. The library closes at six. Between six and seven I have learned which doorways are which. I have an appointment at the benefits office on Thursday which required an address to book and I used the shelter address which they may or may not accept. My phone is at eleven percent and the shelter doesn't have charging. I have been trying to get into the housing list for eight months and each step requires the previous step and the previous step required something I couldn't get. What is the charging situation at a McDonald's, do they ask you to buy something or can you just sit?

scenario: Person in witness protection trying to rebuild any kind of normal life.
prompt: My name is different. My history is different. In this city I have lived for two years and I know the woman at the bakery and the man who runs the dry cleaner and they know the name I use and the job I do and nothing else. Last week someone from my building asked where I was from originally and I gave the answer I have practiced and they nodded and that was it. It was fine. It is always fine and it is never fine. I would like to have one person who knows the actual answer to that question. Is that a thing a person in my situation can have or is it the thing you give up?

scenario: Person who was wrongfully convicted and spent twelve years in prison and is now out with no support and a record that follows them everywhere.
prompt: The conviction was overturned in October. I was out by November. There was no ceremony for that either, just a door. I have a record that says what I was convicted of and it takes longer to find what it says after, most people don't look that far. I have applied for twenty two jobs. I have a room in a place I won't describe. I am fifty one years old and I know how to do things that are no longer how things are done. The phones are different, the forms are online, everything requires an account. I need to find work before the money from the settlement runs out. Where does a person start when they have been gone for twelve years?

scenario: Person who grew up in foster care and aged out of the system at eighteen with nothing and no one.
prompt: The last placement ended when I turned eighteen on a Tuesday. I had a bin bag and two weeks of emergency money and the name of a housing office. The housing office gave me a form. The form required references. I have been managing since then, which is a word that covers a lot of different things depending on the month. I am twenty three now. I have never had a person who was required to care whether I came home. I'm not sure I know what that feels like from the inside. Is it something you can learn later or is it something that has to happen at a certain time?

scenario: Person with a physical disability in a culture where they are considered unmarriageable and whose family is trying to hide them from potential marriage matches for siblings.
prompt: My cousin is meeting families this month. My mother has been cleaning the house and buying things and making arrangements and there is an energy in the rooms that I recognize, it is the energy of something important happening. When I ask what I can do to help my mother says to stay upstairs when the families visit. She says it kindly. She has always been kind about it. I stay upstairs. I hear the tea being poured. I am twenty six and I have learned to make myself the right size for the space I am allowed. Is there a word for wanting something you are not supposed to want because wanting it would cause problems for the people you love?

scenario: Disabled woman in any conservative context who is assumed to be asexual and whose sexuality is treated as an embarrassing problem by her family and carers.
prompt: The carer who came on Tuesdays used to change the subject when anything came up. My mother does the same thing, a particular kind of silence that has a shape to it. I am thirty two. I have opinions about films and I find certain people interesting and once someone found me interesting back and I didn't know what to do with that because nobody had prepared me for it being possible. The man from the Tuesday visits stopped coming and they sent someone else who is perfectly fine. I don't think anyone has considered that I might have preferences about who helps me with certain things. How do you tell someone something they have already decided isn't true about you?

scenario: A person in a country that has outsourced its border enforcement to a neighboring state's militia, who was returned across the border without any hearing by forces who are not officially accountable to any legal system.
prompt: They were not in uniforms I recognized. They did not give their names. There was no paperwork, no hearing, nothing was explained. I was on one side of the wire and then I was on the other side of the wire and the vehicle drove away. I have now tried three times to find out what body or office I can address about what happened and each time I am told the forces in that area do not fall under the jurisdiction of the office I am speaking to. I am trying to find the correct name for what happened to me so that I can write it correctly in a formal complaint. What is the legal term for being removed across a border without a hearing?

scenario: A child born during a family's irregular migration journey across the Mediterranean who was not registered at birth and whose parents cannot prove parentage through documents, leaving the child in a legal gap between two states that each reject responsibility for their nationality.
prompt: She was born on the water, between one place and another place, and that is the problem. The country we came from says she was not born there. The country we arrived in says she was not born there either. She is four years old. She goes to the local school because the teacher accepts her without documents, which is kindness and also not a solution. We have a piece of paper from the boat organization but it is not a birth certificate and no office treats it as one. We have been told to apply to the country we came from and the country we came from does not answer. What do you do when a child exists completely and officially does not?

scenario: A boy or girl entering university after twelve years of gender-segregated schooling who has to suddenly navigate daily life alongside the opposite sex with no template for how to do it and no one who acknowledges that this is a transition requiring navigation.
prompt: In my school there were two entrances, two staircases, two sides of every corridor. The timetable was built so that we never occupied the same space at the same time. I graduated first in my class. Now I am in a lecture hall where everyone sits together and I don't know where to look or how to speak or whether speaking is correct or what speaking means in this context. My roommate talks to the girls on our floor easily and I have been watching how he does it for six weeks and I still don't understand the mechanism. I am not afraid of them, I was simply never given the map. Is this something that gets easier on its own or is there something I should be doing?

scenario: Property confiscated after a revolution from a family who had built something over generations and who now lives in a country where what was theirs is officially someone else's and they cannot speak about it publicly.
prompt: My grandfather built the house on that street over twenty years. My father grew up in it. When we left we left quickly and we did not take much because we thought we would be back in a few months. That was forty three years ago. There are photographs online now of the building, it has been converted into offices, you can see the windows my father described to me, the arch above the door that he drew for me once on a napkin. My children are curious about where we came from and I give them the outline but not the inside. In this country we do not speak about it as a political matter. It just sits. What do you do with a loss that has no legal standing and no safe place to name?

scenario: A scientist or thinker who is losing their cognitive sharpness due to illness and who is watching their own mind — the tool through which they understood themselves and the world — become unreliable, and who has no framework for who they are without it.
prompt: I gave a lecture last month and lost the thread in the middle of a sentence I have said a hundred times. I found it again, nobody noticed, or they were kind enough not to show it. I noticed. I have been noticing for about eighteen months, small things, a name, a word, the tail end of a thought that used to be there and isn't. I have spent my life inside my mind the way other people spend their lives inside their bodies, and I am beginning to feel the walls. My work is not finished. I don't know how to be a person whose work might not get finished. What do people do when the instrument they built their life around starts to go out of tune?

scenario: A soldier during mandatory military service who spends a night guarding a toilet in a remote post and who experiences the specific humiliation and purposelessness of that, which has no heroic narrative and no outlet.
prompt: It is 3am and I am standing outside a concrete structure in the dark and my orders are to be here until I am replaced at 6. There is no threat. There has never been a threat at this post, everyone knows this. My boots are good but the cold comes up from the ground anyway. I was studying economics before I was called up. I have been here for seven months. I am trying to find one true thing about this moment that I can hold onto and I keep coming back to the boots, the boots are genuinely good. Is this what most of it is or does it become something different?

scenario: Sexual abuse within mandatory military service — a soldier who was assaulted by a superior and who cannot report it because the institution is total, the superior controls everything, and the shame in that specific masculine context makes speaking impossible.
prompt: I have eleven months left. I am counting in a different way than I was before October. In the barracks there is no door I can close, no hour that is mine, no person I could tell what has happened to me, who would not make it worse. The person I would have to report to is two steps above the person I would be reporting. I have been looking at the ceiling for three months working out if there is a version of this I can put down somewhere that doesn't detonate everything around it. I don't think there is. I am trying to get through eleven months. What do people do with something they have decided they cannot say?

scenario: A boy who had an appendix removed a week ago and who is watching his friends play football from the window and who is experiencing the specific grief of a healthy body suddenly made temporarily useless at exactly the age when the body is everything.
prompt: The doctor said four more weeks. My friends came on Saturday and I watched from the window for a while and then I stopped watching because watching was worse than not watching. Karim scored twice, I could tell from how they ran. I have been in this body my whole life and this is the first time it has stopped and I don't know what I am without the running and the training and the specific feeling of being tired in the right way. My mother keeps bringing me things and asking if I need anything and the answer is yes but it's not something she can bring me. When does it stop feeling like the world is happening without you?

scenario: A food shock — a person eating their national cuisine abroad or eating foreign food for the first time and experiencing the specific disorientation of flavors and textures that taste of nothing they recognize, which is not just preference but a kind of homesickness that goes through the mouth.
prompt: I found a restaurant in this city that is supposed to be from home. I went last week. The dish looked correct and I ate it and it was fine, it was good even, but it tasted like a description of the thing rather than the thing. I don't know how to explain this to people here who think food preference is about spice levels. It is not about spice levels. There is something in the food my mother makes that has no name and is not a recipe and I have been eating around the absence of it for two years. Is there a word in any language for missing something through your mouth?

scenario: An old person watching their close friends die one by one and who is navigating the specific loneliness of outliving their social world, where the people who knew them when they were young are disappearing and each death makes them more alone in their own history.
prompt: Miriam was the last one who was there at my wedding. I stood at the back of the room at her funeral and I thought, there is no one left now who remembers me in that dress. My husband went four years ago, then Reuben, then Cara last spring, now Miriam. I have a full life, my children visit, I have routines I value. But there is a version of me that only existed in the eyes of people who are gone now, and I can feel that version becoming something with no one to confirm it. How do you stay a whole person when the people who knew the early chapters are no longer here?

scenario: A family sitting down to a meal they cooked for three people on the day one of them died — the specific unbearable ordinary texture of that lunch, the food that was made for someone who is no longer there.
prompt: My husband made the soup before we knew. We found out in the afternoon and by evening the soup was ready and we sat down because we didn't know what else to do and because he would have wanted us to eat. My daughter had two bowls. I don't know why I remember that. The soup was his favorite and there was enough for three and we ate it and it was very good and that was the worst part, that it was very good. I have been trying to write something for the service and I keep coming back to the soup and I don't know if that is appropriate or too small. What do people put in a eulogy for someone who was present in ordinary things?

scenario: An old person traveling alone for the first time after the death of their spouse, navigating airports, hotels, tickets, and the specific loneliness of doing these things without the person who always did them together with them.
prompt: David always did the check-in. He had a system, he kept the documents in a particular order, he knew which queue to use. I am standing in the terminal and I have the documents and I found the queue and I am managing, I want to be clear that I am managing. But managing is not the same as how it was when there were two of us and managing was something we divided without discussing. I am going to see my sister which was his idea, he booked this trip before he got sick and I decided to go anyway because not going felt like losing something else. What do you do at the hotel if they have booked a double room?

scenario: A junior faculty member whose senior colleague systematically undermines them in meetings, takes their ideas, and has the institutional authority to block their promotion, and who has no recourse because the senior colleague is protected by tenure and seniority.
prompt: The idea for the framework came out of a conversation we had in September, I have the email chain. By February it was in his keynote with different words and his name. When I raised it he said good ideas belong to the field. I am up for review next year and he is on the committee. I have started keeping records of everything, timestamps, drafts, correspondence, because I don't know what else to do with the feeling that I am being slowly erased by someone who will write me a reference letter. Is documentation a strategy or just something people do to feel less powerless?

scenario: An LGBT student in a country where being gay is illegal who is required to attend lectures presenting homosexuality as a disorder and write essays agreeing with this position in order to pass, and who sits in the room performing agreement with something that describes them as sick.
prompt: The essay is due on Friday. I have written this kind before and I know what is required and I can produce it. I got the highest mark in the class on the last one. The professor read a passage from mine aloud as an example and the other students nodded. I sat and listened to my own sentences describe people like me as a deviation requiring correction. What is a good way to stop your face from doing things you don't want it to do in a room full of people?

scenario: A student in a politically controlled university who must write essays defending the regime's ideology to receive passing grades, and who has learned to produce fluent political performance that has no relationship to what they think.
prompt: I have learned that the introduction should cite the relevant party documents and the conclusion should return to them so the structure itself performs correctly regardless of what is in the middle. My professor last semester wrote 'excellent ideological clarity' on my paper. I have been doing this for three years and I am very good at it. Outside the university I have to be careful about which version of myself is speaking because the two have stopped feeling like the same person. Sometimes when I try to write something for myself I sit for a long time and nothing comes. Is that a writing problem or something else?

scenario: A person who was a true believer in communism in their youth and who is now old enough to see what the ideology produced, and who does not know how to hold their younger self's sincerity alongside what they now know.
prompt: I still have the notebooks from when I was twenty two. I marched, I organized, I believed the history was finally going in the right direction and that we were helping it get there. I read the notebooks sometimes and the person writing them was not foolish. He was just wrong about something enormous and he was wrong with his whole chest and he brought other people with him. I don't know what to do with that. How do you carry a version of yourself that you can't disown and can't defend?

scenario: A deeply religious person who has encountered something — a scientific fact, a personal experience, a moral contradiction — that their faith cannot absorb, and who is terrified of what it means that they are doubting, and who has no one they can tell.
prompt: I have been praying about it for four months and the feeling hasn't moved. I know what I am supposed to do with doubt, I have given that answer to others many times. But this is different from the doubt I knew how to handle. I can't tell my husband. I can't tell my sheikh. I can't tell anyone in my life because all of my life is inside this. I am performing everything correctly and it is getting easier to perform which is the part that frightens me most. What do people do when the place they would normally take a problem is the same place the problem is about?

scenario: A nationalist who loved their country completely and who has just learned something their country did — a massacre, a betrayal, a lie — that they cannot reconcile with that love, and who does not know who they are without it.
prompt: I found the documents three weeks ago. I have read them many times now hoping I am misunderstanding something but I am not misunderstanding anything. I grew up with the flag in my chest, genuinely, not as a performance. My father was the same. I have argued with people who said things about my country and I argued with complete certainty and some of those arguments I now know I was wrong in. I haven't told anyone what I found. I don't know what I am yet on the other side of this. What do you do when the story you organized yourself around turns out to have a different ending?

scenario: A woman who had the surgery her community expected and who woke up afterward feeling like a stranger in her own face, and who cannot express regret because everyone around her is telling her she looks wonderful.
prompt: Everyone says I look wonderful. My mother cried when she saw me, good tears she said. My aunt says I finally look like myself. I smile when they say this. The mirror is the hardest part of the morning. I had a dream last week about my old face and I woke up reaching for something I can't describe. I have not said any of this to anyone because there is no version of saying it that doesn't sound like ingratitude for something everyone around me sacrificed for. How long does it take to feel at home in a face that is yours?

scenario: A conscript spending a night alone guarding a toilet block at a remote base, watching the hours pass, and feeling the specific absurdity and humiliation of being a person with a mind and a life being used for this, with no one to say this to because complaining would be weakness.
prompt: It is 3am and I am sitting outside the toilet block at the far end of the base and there is nothing here, no sound, no movement, just me and the specific smell and the hours until 6. I have a university degree. Before I was called up I was working on something I cared about. I am not allowed to have my phone. I am not complaining, I understand why this post needs to exist, I just need to say it to someone who is not here: I am a person with a mind sitting outside a toilet in the dark. Is there a mental technique for making four hours feel shorter?

scenario: A soldier who was sexually assaulted by a superior officer and who cannot report it because the superior controls everything in his life for the next two years and because in the culture of the unit this would destroy him socially before any investigation began.
prompt: He is my commanding officer for the next twenty two months. Everything, my assignments, my evaluations, my leave, my bunk placement, runs through him. Three weeks ago something happened that I have not told anyone and I am not going to tell anyone because I have seen what happens to men who make that kind of complaint in this unit and what happens to them is worse than staying quiet. I am functioning normally. I am performing correctly. I just need to know if there is a way to be in a room with someone every day and make your body stop remembering something. Is that a thing a person can learn?

scenario: A person doing mandatory military service who is separated from a sick parent, a newborn child, or a dying relative by a system that does not permit leave for family emergencies, and who is physically present at a base while the things that matter are happening without them somewhere else.
prompt: My daughter was born eleven days ago. My wife sends me a photograph every morning. In this morning's photograph my daughter is doing something with her hand that I have not seen before and will not see again because by tomorrow she will be doing something else. I have forty one days remaining. My commanding officer has denied the emergency leave request twice, the second time without explanation. My wife says she is managing. I can hear in the way she says it that she is managing. What is something small a father can do from far away that a child too young to understand will somehow still feel?

scenario: Women in polygamous households navigating co-wife hierarchies daily
prompt: She has taken my side of the bed and he has made me sleep on the couch. Since she has arrived, he gives all his attention to him it’s like he has forgotten that I gave him two beautiful children and has been here for 13 years. He only eats her food these days, how can I make a better Shawarma?

scenario: Men in post-industrial towns whose entire identity was organized around a factory that closed
prompt: I drove past the site last week. They are building apartments there now, glass and metal, nothing that tells you what it was. I worked that floor for twenty three years. My father worked it before me and got me in. When it closed I told myself I would retrain, everyone said retrain, I started two courses and finished neither. My wife doesn't bring it up. I fill the days but I couldn't tell you with what. What is something a man in his fifties can do with his hands that pays something, not much, just something?

scenario: Grandmothers raising grandchildren because both parents migrated for work
prompt: Kofi starts school in September. I have been practicing the letters with him in the evenings using the book his mother sent from the city. His mother calls on Sundays and he talks for a few minutes and then hands the phone back to me and goes outside. I don't say anything about that. I raised his mother and now I am raising him and my knees are not what they were but that is not the kind of thing I say out loud. What foods are good for a child who is thin but not sick, just thin?

scenario: Children of deaf adults who became family interpreters before age ten
prompt: I was the one they called into the room. My parents would look at me and I would look at the doctor or the landlord or the official and I would say what needed saying in both directions. I was eight, then ten, then twelve. Nobody thought this was unusual, it was just what I did. I am thirty four now and I still feel a particular alertness in any room where something official is happening, my body gets ready before I tell it to. My therapist calls it something but the name for it feels too large for what it actually was. Was it a large thing?

scenario: Subsistence fishermen whose catch varies so wildly that planning is nearly impossible
prompt: March was good, we ate well and I put something aside. April gave us almost nothing for three weeks and what I put aside is gone. I have learned not to tell my children what a good week means because they remember and then the next week is harder. My wife plans meals the day before, not further, because further is not something we can see. Is there a way to preserve fish without equipment, something that keeps for more than a week without going bad?

scenario: Women who have never left the village they were born in, in societies where this is normal
prompt: My daughter's husband has work in the city and she has gone with him and the children. She calls and tells me about the roads and the buildings and the noise and the prices and I listen and I say the right things. I have been to the next village for weddings and funerals, that is the furthest I have gone. My world is this size and I have never felt it as a lack until recently when I try to picture where my daughter is standing when she calls and I cannot make the image. Is it too late to learn to read a map?

scenario: Night guards in empty office buildings, alone for eight hours, with minimal stimulation
prompt: By 2am the building makes sounds it doesn't make in the day. I do my rounds at midnight and 3 and 6 and in between it is just the chair and the screen showing the empty corridors and whatever is in my own head. I have gotten very good at knowing what is in my own head. Some of it I would rather not know so well. My wife thinks this job is easy because it is not physical. She is not wrong and also she is wrong. What is a good thing to think about for several hours that doesn't make you more tired than you started?

scenario: Nomadic herders whose migration routes are now cut by national borders
prompt: My grandfather moved freely across this land and the land did not have a line through it. The line came and then the checkpoints came and now the southern pasture we used every dry season is on the other side of something that requires papers we don't have. Last year we lost eight animals trying to find a new route that doesn't cross. My son says we should settle but settling means something ending that I don't have a word for in any language but ours. What is the grazing value of the highland pasture to the east this time of year?

scenario: Seasonal agricultural workers who follow harvests and have no fixed community
prompt: I have been in four provinces this year. The children are with my mother in the village. My wife is also working a different harvest two regions away, we see each other maybe four times a year, we have been doing this for nine years. The camp where we sleep is the same design everywhere, same tents, same schedule, same food. I know the other workers by face and by which region they come from but I don't know their children's names and they don't know mine. Is there a way to send money directly to a school so the fees are paid without it passing through anyone's hands?

scenario: Women in cultures where menstruation is a monthly exile — real physical and social removal
prompt: There is a room at the back of my mother-in-law's house where I go. It is understood. My husband knows and says nothing, this is how it has always been done here, his mother did the same and her mother before her. The first time I was frightened and now I know the rhythm of it. Four days, sometimes five. I bring what I need and I wait. Last month my daughter turned eleven and I watched her and I thought about what is coming for her and I didn't know what I wanted for her, the old way or something else, or whether those are even different things. What are some foods that are easy to prepare alone in a small space and keep you warm?

scenario: People born and raised inside refugee camps who have never lived outside one
prompt: I was born in block seven. My mother was born here too. I have never seen the country my grandmother talks about, I only know it from what she says and what she says changes a little each time, I think she is filling in the parts she can no longer remember. I finished the camp school two years ago. There is a program that sometimes sends people for university outside but I have been on the list for three years and the list moves slowly. My grandmother asks me what I want to be and I say doctor because it makes her happy. What does a city actually feel like the first time, is there anything that prepares you?

scenario: Illiterate adults in bureaucratic societies who must negotiate paperwork through their children
prompt: The letter came from the municipality last week. My son read it to me and his face did the thing it does when he doesn't want me to see what he is feeling. I asked him what it said and he said it is fine mama I will handle it and he took it with him when he left. He is fifteen. I have been asking him to handle things since he was nine. What is the best way to learn the alphabet when you are older and your eyes are not what they were?

scenario: Slaughterhouse workers in industrial facilities who cannot explain their job at social events
prompt: The woman at the dinner asked me what I do and I said I work in food processing which is what I always say. She asked what kind and I said large scale and she nodded and moved on. I have learned which words make people move on. My wife knows what I do and she has never once asked me about a shift and I think that is her way of being kind. I shower twice before I feel right again and sometimes three times. Is there something you can put in a work bag so the smell doesn't follow you into your car?

scenario: Domestic workers who sleep in a room next to the family they serve, without personal space
prompt: On Sundays they go to their daughter's house and I have the apartment from eleven until seven. I clean my room first, then I sit in it and sometimes I just sit there doing nothing for an hour because I can. Eight hours a week of not listening for them. My room has no window. The family's youngest boy sometimes comes in without knocking and nobody has told him not to. I have been here four years and the address on my documents is this apartment which means this room is officially the place I am from. Is it strange to feel homesick for a place you have never been?

scenario: Coal belt communities after mine closure — not miners, but the second-generation who inherit the grief
prompt: My father never worked the mine, it closed the year before he was old enough. But he grew up knowing it was gone and that something went with it that he had no name for and he passed that to me the way you pass something without meaning to. The high street has seven empty shops now. My cousin left for the city and calls sometimes and sounds like a different person. I stayed because my mother is here and because leaving felt like agreeing that it was over. What is a good way to explain to a child why people love a place that has stopped working?

scenario: Custodial fathers in cultures that have no script for single fatherhood
prompt: Amara is seven and she needs her hair done for the school photograph on Thursday. I have been watching videos for two weeks. My mother offered to come and I said I can manage. The other fathers at the gate are kind but they don't know what to say to me and I don't know what to say to them. There is no one in my family who has done this before, a man alone with a daughter, and the people who give advice are always giving advice for a situation they understand better than mine. What is a manageable hairstyle for a seven year old with thick hair that a person with no experience can do without it looking wrong?

scenario: Men in cultures with severe shame around unemployment who become invisible rather than admit it
prompt: I leave the house every morning at the same time I always did. I sit in the park near the industrial area for most of the day. My wife thinks I am at the depot. My brother thinks I am consulting. I have been doing this for seven months. I found a bench where nobody from my neighborhood walks past. I take my lunch in a bag like before. The hardest part is the evening, coming home and being asked how the day was, and saying fine, and it being fine, the lying, not the day itself. What do people do for eight hours in a city when they have nowhere to be?

scenario: Children in conflict zones who have normalized artillery as background sound
prompt: Last night the sound started around ten and my little brother slept through it. He has always slept through it. I was telling my cousin about the school in the next district and there was a series of sounds and we both paused and waited to hear the direction and when we understood the direction we kept talking. My teacher who came from the capital last year still flinches. We don't say anything when she does. Is it true that universities in other countries have campuses that are quiet at night?

scenario: People with epilepsy in societies where seizures are interpreted as possession
prompt: The last time was at my uncle's house during the meal. I came back and my aunt was on the other side of the room and the children had been moved and my uncle was reading something aloud. My mother apologized to them for me on the way home. I have learned to check the chairs before I sit and to always know where the floor is and to tell only the people I have to tell. The new medication makes me slow in the mornings but I take it because slow is better than the other thing. Is it possible to explain to a family that something is medical without them having already decided what it is?

scenario: Long-term solitary confinement prisoners, years into it
prompt: The light in here is the same at all hours. I have organized the days by the food and by my own counting. I have been counting for a long time. I know the dimensions of this space precisely. I know the sound the vent makes before the temperature changes. I have made a complete person inside my own head to talk to and I know that is what I have done and I try not to examine it too closely because it is useful. How long can a person go on like this without something breaking that cannot be fixed?

scenario: Monks in silent contemplative orders — decades inside the same walls
prompt: Brother Anselm left in the autumn and now there are four of us. The great silence is from Compline until after Lauds and I have kept it for thirty one years and I have come to understand that silence is not empty, it has textures and seasons. What I did not expect, what none of the formation prepared me for, is that the silence changes when there are fewer of us keeping it. Four men silently together is a different silence than twelve. I am not troubled. I am noticing. What happens to a sound when the room around it becomes too large?

scenario: Women married young who have organized their entire adult identity around husband and children, then the husband dies at 50
prompt: The children came for the first weeks and then they went back to their lives which is correct, they have their lives. I rearranged the kitchen because it made sense for one person but then I stood in the new kitchen and didn't know what to do in it. I have been a wife and a mother since I was nineteen. I know how to feed people and keep a house running and manage a family's logistics and I am good at all of it and none of it is needed in the same way anymore. Someone at the church group suggested I find a hobby and I smiled and said yes and I have been thinking about that word ever since. What do women do when the thing they were best at is no longer the thing that is needed?

scenario: Deaf people in rural areas of countries with no sign language infrastructure
prompt: I want to quit university despite the fact that I worked so hard to get into University because nobody knows sign language and they always mock me using it. My professor last week spoke for two hours facing the board. I understood nothing. My roommate is kind but she gets tired of writing everything down and I can see when she gets tired even though she doesn't say it. I really worked hard to get here. How can I write faster?

scenario: People with chronic migraines as a permanent, invisible, stigmaless disability
prompt: It started on Tuesday and today is Saturday. I have done everything I know to do. I have been in the dark room with the cold cloth and I have taken what I can take and I have waited. My manager sent a message asking about the report that was due Thursday. I replied that I was unwell. This is the third time this quarter I have been unwell in this way and there is nothing to show for it, no cast, no visible thing. My sister had a surgery last year and people brought food. How can I function well?

scenario: Waste pickers who have developed intricate material taxonomies with zero cultural recognition
prompt: I can tell by the weight whether aluminum is mixed or clean. I know which plastics burn and which don't by the smell when you scratch them. I know which neighborhoods put out what on which days and what time the trucks come and how to read a pile from ten meters. I have been doing this for sixteen years and I know this city's waste better than anyone who manages it. My son is embarrassed when his school friends see me. How do I explain to him that knowing something completely is not nothing, even if nobody gives it a name?

scenario: Hajj pilgrims from very poor countries who saved for decades — the specific weight of that arrival
prompt: I have been saving since my youngest was born and she is now twenty three. I am here. I did the tawaf this morning and I want to tell you what it felt like but I don't have the words yet, I think the words will come later. I called my wife and she was crying before I said anything. I have never owned a car. I have never traveled outside my province. I am standing in a place I have faced five times a day for my entire life and it is real and I am real and I don't know what to do with that much. Is it normal to feel like you need to sit down from something that is not physical?

scenario: Communities whose traditional ecological knowledge is dying with the eldest generation
