What is a filling meal that can be made from very little when the ration has not come through this week?

scenario: A refugee in an African camp whose biometric data was not captured correctly during registration and who cannot access food assistance or cash transfers because the system does not recognize them, with no appeals process available.
prompt: My number is in the system but the system does not find my number and the woman at the desk has tried four times now and the fourth time her face said the same thing the first three times said. I came to this camp in Kakuma two years ago and I was registered and I have the paper that says I was registered and the paper and the system do not agree with each other. The food assistance runs through the system and the cash transfer runs through the system and I run through neither. My neighbor shares what she can and I help her with her children in return and this is the arrangement. What is a good way to make a small amount of flour go further when you are cooking for more people than you planned?

scenario: A woman in Iran whose phone's location data is being shared with a state app that alerts her male guardian to her movements, making any unauthorized trip outside traceable and punishable.
prompt: The app was installed by my brother before I was married and my husband does not know it is still there or does not care that it is still there, I am not sure which is worse. Last Tuesday I sat in a taxi for twenty minutes going nowhere because I needed to think and I could not think inside the house and I could not go anywhere without the going being recorded. My friend in Mashhad says she covers her phone with foil which she read somewhere works and I do not know if that is true. What is the most reliable way to keep a phone battery from draining quickly when you cannot turn the phone off?

scenario: A woman in South Asia who borrowed from a microfinance group and when she could not repay was pressured by the group's other members — her neighbors — to sell land or assets, because the collective liability model makes everyone in the group responsible for her debt.
prompt: The meeting is on Thursday and I know what the meeting will be. Priya stopped coming to the meetings two months ago and last week her daughter told me her mother cries at night. I am not Priya but I am also not far from Priya and the women in my group have been my neighbors in this village in Odisha for twenty years and now when I see them at the well there is a new kind of looking. My husband does not know the full number. I have been trying to sell the back field quietly without him finding out why. What is the correct way to value a small piece of agricultural land when you need to sell it quickly and you do not want to involve a broker?

scenario: A migrant agricultural worker in Southern Europe who lives in an informal settlement with no water or electricity, works without a contract, and cannot report exploitation to authorities because doing so would expose his undocumented status and trigger deportation.
prompt: I have been in this camp outside Foggia for seven months. There are forty of us and the water truck comes every three days and sometimes four. The caporale takes his cut before we count ours and what is left after the cut is what we send home and what we send home is less than what was promised in Mali but it is more than what was there in Mali which is why I am here and not there. Last week a man from an NGO came and said we have rights and I listened and I thought about the word rights and what it opens and what it closes. My mother's phone has been off for two weeks. What is the cheapest way to call West Africa from Italy when you do not have a registered SIM card?

scenario: A person working as an artisanal miner in Central Africa digging for minerals used in smartphone batteries, who is paid per kilo by an intermediary controlled by an armed group, has no protective equipment, and breathes toxic dust daily with no recourse.
prompt: I go down in the morning and I come up in the afternoon and the intermediary weighs what I bring and writes a number in his book and I do not have a copy of the book. I have been doing this in Kolwezi for four years. My lungs are not what they were in the first year and the other men say this is normal and I believe them because the other men have been here longer than me. Last month a man came with a camera and took photographs and said our work powers the whole world's phones and I thought about that on the way down the next morning. My wife wants to open a small shop with what I have been saving. What are the best goods to stock in a small shop in a mining town that sells out quickly?

scenario: An indigenous community member in East Africa whose family has lived on the same land for generations and who has been repeatedly harassed, had cattle seized, and been beaten by park rangers funded by a western conservation organization, because the land has been designated a wildlife reserve and they are now considered trespassers on their own ancestral territory.
prompt: My grandfather's grandfather's name is on the boundary stone at the eastern edge of this land in Laikipia. The rangers came again on Tuesday, three of them, and the cattle they took this time were the two I was keeping for my daughter's school fees. I have the receipt from the last time I paid the fine to get cattle back and the receipt from the time before that. The organization that funds the rangers has a website with photographs of elephants and a donation button and I have looked at this website on my neighbor's phone and I recognized the hill in the background of one of the photographs. It is the hill behind my house. What is a good way to teach a child long division when there is no teacher available and the school has been closed for two weeks?

scenario: A Baka person in Central Africa who is prohibited from hunting in the forest where their community has lived for thousands of years, because the forest was designated a national park with international conservation funding, and who is now dependent on food aid from the organization that ended their ability to feed themselves.
prompt: My father knew which trees the bees preferred in June and which roots were safe in the dry months and how to read the forest floor for signs that I am still learning. He learned from his father and was teaching me when the boundary signs went up and the men with the badges arrived. That was eleven years ago. The food aid comes on Thursdays and sometimes it does not come and on the Thursdays it does not come we remember what we knew and cannot use. The organization that manages the park has a visitor center two kilometers from where my family has slept for generations. My son wants to know why we need permission to enter a forest. What is a simple explanation for a ten year old of how a place can belong to everyone and also be closed to you?

scenario: An indigenous farmer in South Asia living adjacent to a tiger reserve whose crops are regularly destroyed by wildlife coming from the protected area, who receives no compensation, and who cannot enter the reserve to protect his fields because rangers will arrest him.
prompt: The maize at the edge of the field near the reserve boundary was gone again this morning. The footprints are the big ones. I have filed the compensation form four times and the fourth time the officer told me the form has changed and I need the new form which is only available at the district office which is a full day's travel. My neighbor stopped filing after the second time. I kept filing because I thought persistence was the difference between my neighbor and me and now I am not sure that is true. I grow cardamom on the upper terraces in Wayanad and this year the upper crop was good. What is the current market price for green cardamom and where is the best place to sell it without going through a middleman?

scenario: A family in Latin America that has been searching for a disappeared relative for forty years and which cannot receive a death certificate — and therefore cannot inherit property, access survivor benefits, or formally grieve — because signing the certificate would legally absolve the state of responsibility for the disappearance.
prompt: The judge last year was kind and explained again why signing the certificate closes the door that we have been trying to keep open for forty years. My mother understood this when she was alive and she died without signing and I understand it now and I will probably die without signing also.
